206	## Restyle a caption track
207	
208	A style is fixed when the captions are generated. To change it, generate again with **Replace** ticked:
209	
210	1. Open **File ▸ Generate Captions…** over the same clips.
211	2. Choose the new word style and looks.
212	3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
213	4. Press **Generate**.
214	
215	The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front, all in one undo step. With AssemblyAI the cached transcript is reused, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed.
216	
217	**Replace** is live only for a word style, and only when there is a track it may replace. That means a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. Tracks outside the run's scope are left alone.
218	
219	## Re-lay captions for a new canvas
220	
221	Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on. After you change the canvas size (on the Document tab, or an agent's `set_canvas`), choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** to page them again for the new width.
222	
223	- Every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips is looked at. A track whose pages are all in one of the five word styles Frame Job makes, with its looks, is re-paged from the words its pages hold. Every correction you typed is kept, and nothing is transcribed again.
224	- Each page is re-paged inside its own clip: a page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are, and pages are never merged across clips. Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
225	- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.
226	- A track is **kept as placed** when it is a matte track, holds a page with no word timings (Subtitles, or a page whose word count you changed), holds a page none of whose words starts inside it, holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make, has pages in more than one style, or the new pages would not fit in the project. A sheet after the edit names each kept track and why. Nothing appears when every track was re-laid.
227	- It is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
228	
229	The item is greyed out with no caption track it can re-lay, while a sheet is open, and while a recording runs. Inside a nest it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size. **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy (see [Vertical versions](vertical-and-framing.md)).
230	
231	*Agents:* `relay_captions` does the same in the container `set_scope` has open. It answers the tracks re-laid (`relaid`: the new track, the track it replaced, its name, style and page count) and the tracks kept with their reasons (`kept`). With nothing it can re-lay it is refused, naming each kept track and its reason.
232	
233	## Editing captions
234	
235	Captions are text clips, so the inspector's Clip tab edits them under **Text**: Content, Font, Style, Outline, Backdrop, Box, Reveal and Presets. Select several captions to change them together.
236	
237	On a word caption page:
238	
239	- **Case.** The style's capitals come from **Text ▸ Style ▸ UPPERCASE**. Untick it to show a page as written. Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the Content box shows the words as written, and changing case never drops the word timing.
240	- **Word style colours.** There is no inspector section for a page's word style (highlight colour, pop scale, pill colour). To change them, generate again with a different style, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
241	- **Editing the words.** Changing the text while keeping the same number of words keeps every word's timing. Changing the number of words drops the timing, and the page then shows plainly. The Content section notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". The same rule holds whether you edit in the Content box or in place on the canvas (double-click the page).
242	- **Reveal.** The text reveals (typewriter, word fade, line rise) do not apply to a timed page. The Reveal section says "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
243	- **Trimming and splitting.** These keep each word on the speech it times. Retiming a page by dragging it moves its words with it.
244	
245	*Agents:* `set_text` edits a caption like any text clip, including a page's `words` and `word_style`. When `words` is not empty, it must have exactly one timing for each word of the content. Otherwise the edit is refused: "this text is timed word by word: N timings for M words".
246	
247	## Export captions
248	
249	Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. The item is greyed out unless some track holds only text clips with caption text on them. The save panel suggests *project name*`.srt` and adds two popups:
250	
251	| Control | What it does | Default |
252	|---|---|---|
253	| **Track** | Which track to write, listed as "*name* — N cues (track *id*)", front-most first. Greyed when there is only one candidate. | The front-most candidate |
254	| **Format** | **SubRip (.srt)** or **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Changing it changes the file name's extension. | SubRip (.srt) |
255	
256	Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now, so a caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Empty captions are left out. Line endings become LF, and blank lines inside a caption are removed. The two formats differ only in WebVTT's `WEBVTT` header, its missing index lines, the `.` where SubRip writes `,` in timestamps, and WebVTT escaping `&`, `<` and `>`. Exporting changes nothing in the project.
257	
258	Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips can be exported, a titles track included. A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written: the style's UPPERCASE, its word timings and its styling are not part of a `.srt` or `.vtt`.
259	
260	**Round trips are exact to the frame.** A track exported and imported again puts every cue back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match byte for byte, because import snaps times to the frame grid: at 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`.
261	
262	*Agents:* `export_captions` (`path`, plus optional `track` and `format`). The track is never guessed: with no candidate, or more than one and no `track` given, the call is refused and the candidates are listed. A `.srt` or `.vtt` extension in `path` is replaced by the format's own, and any other extension is kept (`chart.png` becomes `chart.png.srt`).
263	
264	## Your AssemblyAI key
265	
266	The key lives in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,), in the **Transcription** section:
267	
268	| Control | What it does |
269	|---|---|
270	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. "Paste your key" when none is saved. A saved key shows as a fixed row of dots and is never displayed again. Press Return or **Save** to save. |
271	| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**: the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to. Default: United States. The two regions do not share transcripts, so a pending delete is retried only in the region it was made in. |
272	| **Save** | Saves the key typed in the field ("Key saved."). |
273	| **Remove** | Deletes the saved key ("Key removed."). Live only when a key is saved. |
274	| **Verify** | Makes the cheapest signed-in call to AssemblyAI with the key in the field, or the saved key, and answers "Key accepted" or AssemblyAI's reason. It reads "Checking…" while it runs, "No API key is set." with no key, and "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." if the key or region changes mid-check. It does not transcribe or bill anything. |
275	| **Account Page** | Opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in the browser, where you get a key and see your spending. |
276	
277	The key is saved in a file only you can read (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`, mode `0600`), not in the Keychain, and it is never passed on the command line. Saving, removing or changing the region updates an open Generate Captions sheet straight away. The ⓘ beside the heading explains what is uploaded, what is deleted, and the published rate.
278	
279	No MCP tool can read or change the key or the region. Only a person sets them, here.
280	
281	## Limits
282	
283	- **Import reads SubRip only.** WebVTT can be exported but not imported.
284	- Captions are burned-in text clips, not a switchable subtitle stream in the exported movie.
285	- A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio switched off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent cannot be transcribed.
286	- **On this Mac** needs the language's speech model installed from the sheet's Download row. Speakers, Vocabulary and Transcribe again are AssemblyAI only.
287	- **AssemblyAI** needs a key (unless every file is already cached), uploads and bills each whole media file, and refuses a file over 10 hours. Vocabulary is capped at 1,000 terms.
288	- Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
289	- Word styles mark words by their timing only. There is no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
290	- A page's word style colours and scale cannot be edited in the inspector. Generate again, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
291	- Speaker colours apply only to the Subtitles style.
292	- Changing the number of words on a word caption page drops its word timing. To time it again, generate again.
293	- A style cannot be switched on a placed track. Restyle by generating again with Replace.
294	- Re-lay Captions re-pages only word caption tracks in a style Frame Job makes. A Subtitles track keeps its cues as placed; generate again on the new canvas to re-wrap it.
295	
296	## For agents
297	
298	| Tool | Mirrors |
299	|---|---|
300	| `import_captions` | File ▸ Import Captions… |
301	| `transcribe` | File ▸ Generate Captions… |
302	| `export_captions` | File ▸ Export Captions… |
303	| `relay_captions` | File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas |
304	| `get_transcript` | Reads one clip's words with their timeline times, from the cached transcript or this Mac's recogniser. It never uses the network and edits nothing. Used for cutting by transcript ([Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)). |
305	
306	In the built-in [Assistant](assistant.md), `transcribe` with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld, because audio leaves the Mac only when a person chooses that in the sheet. `export_captions` asks before it writes a file. The full reference is [MCP](mcp.md).
307	
308	Filler-word removal, which needs an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words, is covered in [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md). The Settings window as a whole is covered in [Settings](settings.md).

192	        var words: [CaptionCues.Word] = []

204	    /// style's are `CaptionStyle.textProps` at the page's own size and width —

213	                size: preset.size(on: canvas),

228	        let glide = looks.slide && tokens >= 2 ? previewGlide : nil
229	        return [
230	            RecipeReveal(word: 1, wordPop: 1, wordFill: fill),
231	            RecipeReveal(word: min(2, tokens), wordPop: 1, wordGlide: glide, wordFill: fill),
232	        ]
233	    }

235	    /// The sample page drawn by the renderer: two frames for a word style
236	    /// (`previewReveals`), one for Subtitles, each
237	    /// scaled to fit a 258×36 slot, stacked 8 pt apart over the plate, at 2×.
238	    func preview() -> NSImage? {
239	        let canvas = CGSize(width: snapshot.canvas.width, height: snapshot.canvas.height)
240	        let frame = max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
241	        guard
242	            let cue = CaptionPages.samplePage(
243	                sampleWords(), request: pagesRequest, frame: frame)
244	        else { return nil }
245	        let props = previewProps(for: cue, canvas: canvas)
246	        let reveals =
247	            style.isWordStyle
248	            ? Self.previewReveals(tokens: props.tokenCount, looks: looks)
249	            : [RecipeReveal.whole]
250	        let size = Self.previewSize
251	        let scale: CGFloat = 2
252	        guard
253	            let context = LayerRenderers.bitmap(
254	                CGSize(width: size.width * scale, height: size.height * scale))
255	        else { return nil }
256	        context.setFillColor(DS.captionPreviewPlate.cgColor)
257	        context.fill(CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: context.width, height: context.height))
258	        context.scaleBy(x: scale, y: scale)
259	        context.interpolationQuality = .high
260	
261	        let slot = CGSize(width: size.width, height: 36)
262	        let gap: CGFloat = 8
263	        let count = CGFloat(reveals.count)
264	        // From the TOP, in points; the context is y-up.
265	        var top = (size.height - count * slot.height - (count - 1) * gap) / 2
266	        for reveal in reveals {
267	            if let bitmap = LayerRenderers.textBitmap(props, reveal: reveal),
268	                let image = bitmap.makeImage()
269	            {
270	                let fit = min(
271	                    slot.width / CGFloat(image.width), slot.height / CGFloat(image.height))
272	                let drawn = CGSize(
273	                    width: CGFloat(image.width) * fit, height: CGFloat(image.height) * fit)
274	                context.draw(
275	                    image,
276	                    in: CGRect(
277	                        x: (size.width - drawn.width) / 2,
278	                        y: size.height - top - slot.height + (slot.height - drawn.height) / 2,
279	                        width: drawn.width, height: drawn.height))
280	            }
281	            top += slot.height + gap
282	        }
283	        guard let image = context.makeImage() else { return nil }
284	        return NSImage(cgImage: image, size: size)
285	    }
286	}

3	/// Cues in, ops out — the half of caption import that has nothing to do with
4	/// SubRip, factored out of `CaptionImporter.swift` so the speech recogniser
5	/// (`Transcriber.swift`) lays its captions out exactly as an imported file's
6	/// are laid out. A caption is an ordinary text clip either way, and
7	/// `CaptionImporter`'s header doc is still where the reasoning for THAT lives.
8	///
9	/// **What is here is PLACEMENT, and only placement.** Road map 2 phase 4 says
10	/// the cue rules — at most two lines, at most 42 characters a line, at most
11	/// six seconds a cue, at least a frame between cues, and (road map 6 §5f) no
12	/// two speakers in one cue: five of them now — are "factored out
13	/// of `CaptionImporter.swift`". None of them was ever in that file: SubRip
14	/// supplies its own line breaks, the clip's `text.width` does the wrapping at
15	/// render time (`LayerRenderers.measure`), and the importer bounds no cue's
16	/// length. Moving those rules in here would silently re-wrap and re-time every
17	/// caption file people already import, and would break the 4b round trip
18	/// outright. So the five rules belong to the producer that has to invent line
19	/// breaks — the transcriber's cue builder — and this file does what the
20	/// importer actually did:
21	///
22	/// 1. snap each cue to the canvas frame grid (spec §5.1: the model never
23	///    stores a sub-frame time);
24	/// 2. give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back;
25	/// 3. sort by start, ties broken by the order the producer emitted them;
26	/// 4. cut an overlapping cue back to **abut** its successor — never to leave a
27	///    gap, because `b.start == a.end` is not an overlap (`transition.rs`), so
28	///    an abutting pair places cleanly and mints no `cross_dissolve`, while a
29	///    real overlap would both be refused by §6's rule and dissolve between two
30	///    captions if it were not;
31	/// 5. drop — and REPORT — whatever is then shorter than a frame;
32	/// 6. put the survivors on a new front-most track, which is the one placement
33	///    the overlap rule can never refuse, in the Caption preset.
34	///
35	/// **Problems are reported, never dropped.** A caption run half of which
36	/// vanished without a word is worse than one that did not happen, so every
37	/// refusal keeps the `tag` its producer gave it — `"line 12"` for a file,
38	/// `"clip 7"` or a timecode for a transcript — and `Problem.description` is
39	/// `"<tag>: <reason>"`, which is what `import_captions` already reports under
40	/// `skipped`.
41	enum CaptionLayout {
42	
43	    // MARK: - Vocabulary
44	
45	    /// One cue as its producer means it, before the frame grid and before its
46	    /// neighbours have had their say.
47	    ///
48	    /// `tag` replaces the SubRip-only line number the importer used to carry:
49	    /// it is whatever names this cue in a message, and it is the producer's to
50	    /// spell, so a parser says `"line 12"` and a transcript says `"clip 7 at
51	    /// 0:04.2"`. Nothing here parses it.
52	    ///
53	    /// The last three are a word caption's page (road map 8's W4a) and nil
54	    /// from every other producer: `words`, one per whitespace token of
55	    /// `text` in TIMELINE ticks; `size`, a lone word's shrunk font size;
56	    /// `width`, the box a lone word too wide even at the floor wraps in.
57	    /// `speaker` is nil from every producer but `CaptionCues.build`, and a
58	    /// Subtitles cue that carries one is placed in its palette colour
59	    /// (spec §11 R6-22).
60	    struct Cue: Equatable {
61	        let start: Ticks
62	        let end: Ticks
63	        let text: String
64	        let tag: String
65	        let words: [CaptionCues.Word]?
66	        let size: Double?
67	        let width: Double?
68	        let speaker: Speaker?
69	
70	        init(
71	            start: Ticks, end: Ticks, text: String, tag: String,
72	            words: [CaptionCues.Word]? = nil, size: Double? = nil, width: Double? = nil,
73	            speaker: Speaker? = nil
74	        ) {
75	            self.start = start
76	            self.end = end
77	            self.text = text
78	            self.tag = tag
79	            self.words = words
80	            self.size = size
81	            self.width = width
82	            self.speaker = speaker
83	        }
84	    }
85	
86	    /// Who said a cue: a label within ONE media's transcript (R6-3), since
87	    /// AssemblyAI letters each file's speakers afresh (spec §11 R6-22).
88	    struct Speaker: Hashable {
89	        let media: UInt32?
90	        let label: String
91	    }
92	
93	    /// A cue its producer refused, or one placement gave up on.
94	    struct Problem: Equatable {
95	        let tag: String
96	        let reason: String
97	
98	        var description: String { "\(tag): \(reason)" }
99	    }
100	
101	    /// What a caption run will do, before anything is applied: the ops, and
102	    /// everything the caller has to tell the user about.
103	    struct Plan {
104	        /// One `add_track` (unless placing on an existing track), one
105	        /// `add_text_clip` per surviving cue, and one `set_video` putting the
106	        /// whole batch where the Caption preset lives.
107	        let ops: [ReelOp]
108	        /// Clips this plan really creates — smaller than `cues` if the core
109	        /// refused a placement on a track the caller chose.
110	        let clips: Int
111	        /// Cues that survived the producer and placement.
112	        let cues: Int
113	        /// Cues shortened because the next one started before they ended.
114	        let trimmed: Int
115	        let problems: [Problem]
116	        /// The name of the track created for these captions; nil when the
117	        /// caller named a track to place them on instead.
118	        let trackName: String?
119	        /// The caption tracks this plan removes, with their clips, before
120	        /// it adds its own — the restyle step (road map 8 §5e). Empty
121	        /// unless the caller asked for it.
122	        let replaced: [UInt32]
123	        /// Subtitles cues that measure over two lines on a canvas taller than wide (spec §11
124	        /// VR-41); 0 on every other canvas and for every word style.
125	        let overTwoLines: Int
126	
127	        /// The human report: what was adjusted and what was skipped. Empty
128	        /// when everything landed cleanly, which is the signal to say nothing
129	        /// at all.
130	        var report: String {
131	            var lines: [String] = []
132	            if trimmed > 0 {
133	                lines.append(
134	                    "\(trimmed) caption\(trimmed == 1 ? "" : "s") overlapped the next one and "
135	                        + "\(trimmed == 1 ? "was" : "were") shortened to fit.")
136	            }
137	            if !problems.isEmpty {
138	                lines.append(
139	                    "\(problems.count) entr\(problems.count == 1 ? "y was" : "ies were") "
140	                        + "skipped:")
141	                lines.append(contentsOf: problems.prefix(8).map { "    • " + $0.description })
142	                if problems.count > 8 {
143	                    lines.append("    • …and \(problems.count - 8) more.")
144	                }
145	            }
146	            if overTwoLines > 0 {
147	                lines.append(
148	                    "\(overTwoLines) caption\(overTwoLines == 1 ? " wraps" : "s wrap") to more "
149	                        + "than two lines on this canvas.")
150	            }
151	            return lines.joined(separator: "\n")
152	        }
153	    }
154	
155	    /// Why a placement produced nothing. These carry no file, because the
156	    /// producer is not always a file: `CaptionImporter` catches them and
157	    /// rewraps the first two into its own URL-carrying cases so the alert
158	    /// text and the tool's error string are unchanged.
159	    enum LayoutError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
160	        /// Nothing survived. The problems are carried so the message can name
161	        /// the first few reasons.
162	        case noCues([Problem])
163	        /// The core refused the whole batch — an `add_text_clip` onto a track
164	        /// the caller named, in practice.
165	        case refused
166	        /// More captions than the project has room for. Refused HERE rather
167	        /// than left to `format::check_caps`, which would throw
168	        /// "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)" halfway through the batch — a
169	        /// true sentence that tells a user nothing about captions, when the
170	        /// count is a fact this plan knows before it builds a single op.
171	        case tooMany(cues: Int, room: Int)
172	
173	        var errorDescription: String? {
174	            switch self {
175	            case .noCues(let problems):
176	                let detail = problems.prefix(3).map { $0.description }.joined(separator: "; ")
177	                return "No captions could be placed on the timeline."
178	                    + (detail.isEmpty ? "" : " \(detail).")
179	            case .refused:
180	                return "The captions could not be placed on the timeline."
181	            case .tooMany(let cues, let room):
182	                return "\(cues) captions is more than this project has room for: "
183	                    + "\(room) more clip\(room == 1 ? "" : "s") would fit, out of "
184	                    + "\(Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS))."
185	            }
186	        }
187	    }
188	
189	    // MARK: - Style
190	
191	    /// The Caption preset of §4.2 — the same row the Text pane's Presets
192	    /// section applies, looked up by name so the two cannot drift. The
193	    /// fallback is that row's own values, and exists only so a rename in
194	    /// `TextPane` is a wrong style rather than a crash.
195	    static var captionPreset: TextPreset {
196	        TextPreset.all.first { $0.name == "Caption" }
197	            ?? TextPreset(
198	                name: "Caption", font: "SourceSans3-Regular", sizeFraction: 0.035, xFraction: 0,
199	                yFraction: 0.38, align: "center",
200	                backdrop: BackdropProps(color: [0, 0, 0, 0.6], padding: 12, radius: 8),
201	                tallYFraction: 0.25)
202	    }
203	
204	    /// How much of the canvas width a caption may fill before it wraps.
205	    /// Unlike the Text pane's presets this plan DOES fix a box width: a
206	    /// caption's words come out of a file or a microphone rather than from
207	    /// someone watching the canvas, so a long line has to wrap itself.
208	    static let wrapFraction = 0.8
209	
210	    // MARK: - Placement
211	
212	    /// A cue once the frame grid and its neighbours have had their say.
213	    private struct Placed {
214	        let tag: String
215	        /// The cue's index in the input, which is how a tie on `start` is
216	        /// broken. The importer used to break it on the SubRip line number;
217	        /// a parser emits its cues in file order and line numbers strictly
218	        /// increase, so the two orders are the same one — and this one also
219	        /// works for a producer whose tags are not numbers at all.
220	        let order: Int
221	        let start: Ticks
222	        var end: Ticks
223	        let text: String
224	        let words: [CaptionCues.Word]?
225	        let size: Double?
226	        let width: Double?
227	        let speaker: Speaker?
228	    }
229	
230	    /// Everything a caption run will do, computed against `project` and
231	    /// applied by nobody: the UI commits it through `ProjectDocument`, the
232	    /// agent through `AgentServer.editResult`.
233	    ///
234	    /// `existing` is whatever the producer already refused — a malformed SubRip
235	    /// block, an ineligible clip — and rides along so one report carries both
236	    /// halves.
237	    ///
238	    /// `track` places on an existing track; absent, the captions get a new
239	    /// front-most track of their own, which is the only placement that can
240	    /// never be refused by the overlap rule.
241	    ///
242	    /// `style` is the caption style (road map 8's W4a). `.subtitles` is the
243	    /// Caption preset and the code path this function always had, byte for
244	    /// byte for a cue with no speaker; a speaker's cue adds its palette
245	    /// `color` (`CaptionStyle.speakerColors`, spec §11 R6-22). A word
246	    /// style writes `style.pagePatch` per page — the props the pager measured,
247	    /// at the page's own size (a shrunk one or the style's), with its wrap
248	    /// width and its `words` in CLIP time — and puts the batch at the style's
249	    /// `y`, with the run's `looks` (W-15). `replacing` names caption tracks to remove
250	    /// WITH their clips in the same ops, first — `replaceableTracks` says
251	    /// which qualify — and the new track takes their place at the front.
252	    static func place(
253	        _ cues: [Cue], problems existing: [Problem] = [], in project: ReelProject,
254	        track: UInt32? = nil, trackBase: String = "Captions", style: CaptionStyle = .subtitles,
255	        looks: CaptionLooks = .none, replacing: [UInt32] = []
256	    ) throws -> Plan {
257	        let snapshot = project.snapshot
258	        let canvas = snapshot.canvas
259	        let frame = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
260	        guard !cues.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(existing) }
261	
262	        // Snap, then give a cue that snapped to nothing its one frame back,
263	        // THEN resolve overlaps — in that order, so an overlap the minimum
264	        // length introduces is still one the overlap pass fixes.
265	        var placed = cues.enumerated().map { index, cue -> Placed in
266	            let start = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(0, cue.start), fps: canvas.fps)
267	            let end = ReelTime.snapToFrame(cue.end, fps: canvas.fps)
268	            return Placed(
269	                tag: cue.tag, order: index, start: start, end: max(end, start + frame),
270	                text: cue.text, words: cue.words, size: cue.size, width: cue.width,
271	                speaker: cue.speaker)
272	        }
273	        placed.sort { $0.start == $1.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.start < $1.start }
274	
275	        // Captions are one track, so two cues on screen at once cannot both
276	        // be honoured: the later one wins its start and the earlier one is
277	        // cut back to it. That is also what the overlap rule (§6) would
278	        // otherwise refuse the placement over.
279	        var trimmed = 0
280	        for index in placed.indices.dropLast() where placed[index].end > placed[index + 1].start {
281	            placed[index].end = placed[index + 1].start
282	            trimmed += 1
283	        }
284	        var problems = existing
285	        for cue in placed where cue.end - cue.start < frame {
286	            problems.append(
287	                Problem(tag: cue.tag, reason: "starts less than a frame before the next caption"))
288	        }
289	        let kept = placed.filter { $0.end - $0.start >= frame }
290	        guard !kept.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.noCues(problems) }
291	
292	        // Before a single op: every op runs `Project::validate`, so a
293	        // transcript one clip too long would throw about clips, halfway
294	        // through, with the earlier ones already applied purely and thrown
295	        // away. The count is known here.
296	        let removed = Set(replacing)
297	        let room = Int(RC_MAX_CLIPS) - snapshot.clips.filter { !removed.contains($0.track) }.count
298	        guard kept.count <= room else {
299	            throw LayoutError.tooMany(cues: kept.count, room: max(0, room))
300	        }
301	
302	        // The replaced tracks go FIRST, clips and all: a removal mints no
303	        // id, so `next_id` below is still the new track's, and the new
304	        // track's index counts the stack as it will be once they are gone.
305	        var ops: [ReelOp] = replacing.map { .removeTrack(track: $0, withClips: true) }
306	        let destination: UInt32
307	        let name = trackName(in: snapshot, base: trackBase, excluding: replacing)
308	        if let track = track {
309	            destination = track
310	        } else {
311	            // A new id is `next_id` from BEFORE the op — the documented
312	            // contract of the one JSON entry point (§6), since an op returns
313	            // a project rather than an id. Index `tracks.count` is the front
314	            // of the stack, so captions draw over everything.
315	            destination = snapshot.nextId
316	            ops.append(.addTrack(index: snapshot.tracks.count - replacing.count, name: name))
317	        }
318	
319	        let preset = captionPreset
320	        let height = Double(canvas.height)
321	        let size = CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height)
322	        var overTwoLines = 0
323	        if style.isWordStyle {
324	            let base = style.size(for: CGSize(width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height))
325	            for cue in kept {
326	                let words = cue.words.map { words in
327	                    words.map { TextWord(start: $0.start - cue.start, end: $0.end - cue.start) }
328	                }
329	                ops.append(
330	                    .addTextClip(
331	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
332	                        text: style.pagePatch(
333	                            content: cue.text, size: cue.size ?? base, width: cue.width,
334	                            words: words, looks: looks)))
335	            }
336	        } else {
337	            var base = TextPatch(
338	                font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: size),
339	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: .some(preset.backdrop),
340	                width: .some(Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction))
341	            if canvas.height > canvas.width {
342	                overTwoLines = kept.filter { measuresOverTwoLines($0.text, preset, on: size) }
343	                    .count
344	            }
345	            let colors = CaptionStyle.speakerColors(kept.map(\.speaker))
346	            for (cue, color) in zip(kept, colors) {
347	                base.content = cue.text
348	                base.color = color
349	                ops.append(
350	                    .addTextClip(
351	                        track: destination, at: cue.start, duration: cue.end - cue.start,
352	                        text: base))
353	            }
354	        }
355	
356	        // The preset's position is a `set_video` patch, and a patch needs
357	        // ids the ops have not minted yet — so the batch is applied PURELY
358	        // first and the ids read off the throwaway result. Applying the same
359	        // ops to the same handle mints the same ids, which is what makes
360	        // appending the patch to this very list correct
361	        // (`EditorViewController+AddClips.swift` does the same for one clip).
362	        //
363	        // The probe is kept rather than replaced by arithmetic on `next_id`:
364	        // ids ARE sequential when nothing is refused, and that is exactly the
365	        // invariant a refusal breaks — a caller-named track can refuse any
366	        // number of these placements, and then the patch would name clips
367	        // that do not exist.
368	        guard let probed = try project.applying(ops).project else { throw LayoutError.refused }
369	        let before = Set(snapshot.clips.map { $0.id })
370	        let created = probed.snapshot.clips.map { $0.id }.filter { !before.contains($0) }
371	        guard !created.isEmpty else { throw LayoutError.refused }
372	        let at = preset.position(on: size)
373	        ops.append(
374	            .setVideo(
375	                clips: created,
376	                patch: style.isWordStyle
377	                    ? VideoPatch(x: 0, y: style.yFraction * height)
378	                    : VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)))
379	
380	        return Plan(
381	            ops: ops, clips: created.count, cues: kept.count, trimmed: trimmed,
382	            problems: problems, trackName: track == nil ? name : nil, replaced: replacing,
383	            overTwoLines: overTwoLines)
384	    }
385	
386	    /// Whether a Subtitles cue, as `place` writes it on `canvas` (the Caption preset, its
387	    /// wrap box), measures taller than the same props holding two lines (spec §11 VR-41).
388	    static func measuresOverTwoLines(
389	        _ content: String, _ preset: TextPreset, on canvas: CGSize
390	    ) -> Bool {
391	        func props(_ text: String) -> TextProps {
392	            TextProps(
393	                content: text, font: preset.font, size: preset.size(on: canvas),
394	                align: preset.align, valign: "middle", backdrop: preset.backdrop,
395	                width: Double(canvas.width) * wrapFraction)
396	        }
397	        return LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props(content)).height
398	            > LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for: props("X\nX")).height
399	    }
400	
401	    /// The tracks a restyle may replace (road map 8 §5e's three rules): a
402	    /// track named as this file names caption tracks ("Captions",
403	    /// "Captions N"), holding at least one clip and only text clips, each overlapping
404	    /// some job's `span` — so nothing outside the run's scope is removed.
405	    static func replaceableTracks(
406	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, jobs: [Transcriber.Job]
407	    ) -> [UInt32] {
408	        snapshot.tracks.compactMap { track -> UInt32? in
409	            guard isCaptionTrackName(track.name) else { return nil }
410	            guard snapshot.clips.contains(where: { $0.track == track.id }) else { return nil }
411	            for clip in snapshot.clips where clip.track == track.id {
412	                guard case .text = clip.source else { return nil }
413	                let end = clip.start + clip.duration
414	                guard jobs.contains(where: { $0.span.overlaps(clip.start ..< end) }) else {
415	                    return nil
416	                }
417	            }
418	            return track.id
419	        }
420	    }
421	
422	    /// A name this file gives a caption track: "Captions" or "Captions N".
423	    static func isCaptionTrackName(_ name: String) -> Bool {
424	        if name == "Captions" { return true }
425	        guard name.hasPrefix("Captions ") else { return false }
426	        let suffix = name.dropFirst("Captions ".count)
427	        return !suffix.isEmpty && suffix.allSatisfy { $0.isASCII && $0.isNumber }
428	    }
429	
430	    /// "Captions", then "Captions 2" — so two runs are tellable apart in the
431	    /// track header. `base` is the producer's word for what it made, and both
432	    /// producers say "Captions": a transcript and an imported file are the
433	    /// same thing on the timeline, and a second name would only make the
434	    /// numbering restart.
435	    /// A track in `excluding` is one this plan removes, so its name is free.
436	    static func trackName(
437	        in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, base: String = "Captions", excluding: [UInt32] = []
438	    ) -> String {
439	        let taken = Set(snapshot.tracks.filter { !excluding.contains($0.id) }.map { $0.name })
440	        var name = base
441	        var suffix = 2
442	        while taken.contains(name) {
443	            name = "\(base) \(suffix)"
444	            suffix += 1
445	        }
446	        return name
447	    }
448	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

core/src/edit_track.rs:218:    pub fn remove_track(&self, track: u32, with_clips: bool) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
        // less than two frames apart cannot have both — recognised words do
        // not do that, but if one ever did, the cue is left short and
        // `CaptionLayout.place` reports and drops it by the rule it already
        // has, rather than being silently dropped here.
        for index in raw.indices.dropLast() {
            raw[index].end = min(raw[index].end, raw[index + 1].start - frame)
        }

        return raw.map { entry in
            CaptionLayout.Cue(
                start: entry.start, end: entry.end, text: entry.lines.joined(separator: "\n"),
                tag: tag(at: entry.start, clip: clip),
                speaker: entry.speaker.map { CaptionLayout.Speaker(media: media, label: $0) })
        }
    }

    /// How a cue names itself in a problem message. A transcript has no line
    /// numbers, so it says where in the timeline it came from and, when the
    /// producer knew, which clip.
    private static func tag(at start: Ticks, clip: UInt32?) -> String {
        let when = String(format: "%.1f s", ReelTime.seconds(start))
        guard let clip = clip else { return "caption at \(when)" }
        return "clip \(clip) at \(when)"
    }
}

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: Subtitles
description: Turn speech into classic two-line captions, give each speaker a colour, and see how the Caption preset sizes and places them on any canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Subtitles style turns speech into classic two-line cues, the kind you'd see on a film or a broadcast. Each cue is a text clip in the **Caption** preset.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style: ▸ Subtitles"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Nothing for the cues themselves. Speaker colours need AssemblyAI."
/>

<Shot
  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Style set to Subtitles. The three look checkboxes and Replace are greyed out, and the preview shows “This is how it looks” in small white text on a dark backdrop."
/>

## Make subtitles

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.

3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles**. The sheet opens on the last style you chose, and on Subtitles the first time.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

The cues land on a new track at the front of the stack, called **Captions**, or **Captions 2** and so on if that name is taken. The whole run is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.

## The Subtitles style

Frame Job builds each cue from the recognised words by these rules:

| Rule | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Lines in a cue | At most 2 |
| Characters on a line | At most 42 |
| Time on screen | At most 6 seconds, up to the end of the cue's last word |
| Gap between cues | At least one frame |
| Speakers in a cue | One. A change of speaker always starts a new cue. |

A cue starts on its first word and ends with its last, so it doesn't stay up through a long silence. A word too long for a line is left whole, never hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.

## Speaker colours

Each speaker's cues can take their own colour, so a viewer can tell who's talking.

<Steps>

1. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:** row is hidden with **On this Mac**.

2. Tick **Speakers:**, which reads "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles".

3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles** and choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

Speakers take their colours in the order they first appear in the run: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. The fifth speaker is white like the first. The colours are a fixed table with no setting. To change one afterwards, select those cues and set the colour under **Text** in the [Clip tab](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).

Speakers are told apart within each media file, so the first speaker in one file and the first speaker in another count as two people and take two colours.

Speaker colours only apply to the Subtitles style. In a [word caption style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), a change of speaker starts a new page and the colours stay as the style draws them.

## The Caption preset

Every cue is drawn in the **Caption** [text preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), whether it was generated or [imported from a SubRip file](/captions/import-captions/).

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Typeface | Source Sans 3 Regular |
| Size | 3.5% of the canvas's shorter side |
| Alignment | Centred |
| Colour | White, unless a speaker colour applies |
| Backdrop | Black at 60%, with 12 px of padding and 8 px corners |
| Wraps at | 80% of the canvas width |
| Position on a wide or square canvas | The box is centred 38% of the frame height below the middle |
| Position on a canvas taller than wide | The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle |

On a 1920 × 1080 canvas that's 38 px text that wraps at 1,536 px. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas it's the same 38 px text, wrapping at 864 px, and a tall canvas such as 9:16 or 4:5 lifts the box to keep it clear of the bottom of the frame.

A narrow canvas can wrap a cue past two lines, because the wrap happens inside the box after the cue is built. On a canvas taller than wide, Frame Job counts these and tells you once the captions are placed:

> 3 captions wrap to more than two lines on this canvas.

After generating, this appears on the sheet, which stays open with **Close**. After importing, it's an alert. The captions are placed either way.

## Good to know

- An imported SubRip file keeps its own line breaks and timing. The rules in [The Subtitles style](#the-subtitles-style) only apply to generated cues.
- **Replace:** is greyed out with Subtitles chosen. To swap a word caption track for Subtitles, generate the new track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
- [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) keeps a Subtitles track as placed. To re-wrap one for a new canvas, generate it again on that canvas.
- A cue has no word timing, so the [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) don't apply. All three boxes are greyed out with Subtitles chosen.
- Subtitles are text in the picture, not a track a player can switch off. To ship a separate file, use [Export Captions…](/captions/export-captions/).

## With an agent

`transcribe` makes Subtitles unless it asks for another style, whatever the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

---
title: Word caption styles
description: Make the large word-by-word captions used in shorts and reels, choose how the spoken word is marked, and see how pages are filled for your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The five word styles make the large, one-row captions used in shorts and reels, where each word is marked as it's said.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style:"
  tools="transcribe"
/>

## Make word captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.

3. Set **Style:** to **Highlight**, **Pill**, **Karaoke**, **Build** or **One Word**. The sheet remembers your choice for next time.

4. Tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) you want, and check the [preview](#the-sheets-two-frame-preview).

5. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

## Word caption pages

A word style doesn't make cues. Each clip holds a **page** of words, with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. A page is still an ordinary [text clip](/captions/how-captions-work/), so you can drag, trim and split it.

All five styles are white with the spoken word marked. Words are marked by their timing only, so there's no keyword emphasis and no emoji.

The text is 7.5% of the canvas's shorter side, or 12% for One Word. That means a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height: on both 1080 × 1920 and 1920 × 1080 it's 81 px, or 130 px for One Word. Where a style pops the spoken word, the pop takes 0.12 s.

## The five styles

### Highlight

The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.

Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Pill

The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.

Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Karaoke

Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55%.

Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.

### Build

Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.

Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### One Word

One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.

Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.

## Bundled typefaces

Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.

## Pages are filled to their measured width

A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.

So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) fills the pages again.

When a page fills up by width and the next page would be much shorter, Frame Job can move the last word across so the two come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.

## Where a page breaks

A page ends early at any of these:

- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked

When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.

On-device words rarely carry a pause, because the recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it. Pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.

## A word too wide for the frame

A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.

## How long a page stays up

A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.

Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.

## The sheet's two-frame preview

The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
| One frame | Subtitles. |
| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |

**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.

## Good to know

- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the sixth choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.

## With an agent

`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

### Highlight

The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.

Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Pill

The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.

Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Karaoke

Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55%.

Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.

### Build

Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.

Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### One Word

One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.

Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.

## Bundled typefaces

Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.

## Pages are filled to their measured width

A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.

So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) fills the pages again.

When a page fills up by width and the next page would be much shorter, Frame Job can move the last word across so the two come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.

## Where a page breaks

A page ends early at any of these:

- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked

When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.

On-device words rarely carry a pause, because the recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it. Pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.

## A word too wide for the frame

A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.

## How long a page stays up

A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.

Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.

## The sheet's two-frame preview

The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
| One frame | Subtitles. |
| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |

**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.

## Good to know

- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the sixth choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.

## With an agent

`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
