---
title: Looks for word captions
description: Add a sliding pill, a left-to-right word fill or a dim in pauses to word captions, and find out what you can change about their colours.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Looks add movement to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/)'s pages: a pill that slides between words, a word that fills as it's said, and a page that dims when nobody's talking.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet, under Style:"
  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
/>

## Three looks for word captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Style:** to a word style.

3. Tick the looks you want under the **Style:** pop-up.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

Each look works with some styles and not others:

| Look | Highlight | Pill | Karaoke | Build | One Word |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Slide the pill** | | Yes | | | |
| **Fill words as spoken** | Yes | | Yes | Yes | |
| **Dim in pauses** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

A box that doesn't apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but it keeps its tick for when you switch back. With **Subtitles** chosen, all three are greyed out.

Each box is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs.

A look changes how a word is drawn, never a letter or the size of the page. Ticking one doesn't change where pages break.

Looks are set when the captions are generated, like the style. To change them on a placed track, [generate again with Replace](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again).

## Slide the pill

The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, instead of jumping. The slide takes 0.2 s, or less when the next word starts sooner, so the pill has always arrived before it has to leave. The first word on a page has nothing to slide from, so the pill starts there.

This works with **Pill**, the only style that has one.

## Fill words as spoken

The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken. The fill runs from the word's start to its end, and takes 0.6 s at most, so a long word finishes filling before it's finished being said.

| Style | The part already said | The rest of the word |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Highlight** | Yellow | White |
| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% |
| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |

**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.

## Dim in pauses

The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.

The page also dims:

- before the first word, when that word starts late. The page opens dim, with no fade.
- after the last word, until the caption ends.

A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.

The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.

## Word colours

The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.

To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or have an agent do it.

The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works. It changes the words drawn in the text's own colour, such as the unmarked words in **Highlight**, and leaves the marked word as it is.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.

It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

---
title: Restyle a caption track
description: Switch a caption track to another word style or look by generating it again, or change the font and backdrop of a run of captions in the inspector.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

There are two ways to restyle captions, depending on what you want to change. A word style and its looks are set when the captions are generated, so changing those means generating again. Font, outline and backdrop are ordinary text settings, which you can change on a run of captions in the inspector.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where={['The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Replace:', 'Clip tab ▸ Text']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
/>

## Restyle by generating again

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and set **From:** to the same clips.

2. Choose the new word style and [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/).

3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front of the stack, all in one undo step, **Generate Captions**. The new track takes the first free name, so a lone **Captions** track is replaced by another called **Captions**.

What it costs depends on the engine:

- **AssemblyAI:** the cached transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
- **On this Mac:** the audio is recognised again. It's free, but it takes the time again.

:::caution
New pages are made from the transcript, not from the old track. Words you corrected, pages you split or trimmed, and anything you restyled by hand go with the old track. To page a track again and keep your corrections, use [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) instead.
:::

## Which tracks Replace may remove

**Replace:** is live only for a word style, and only when there's a track it may replace. It's greyed out with Subtitles chosen. When it isn't live, it's unticked and the line under it is hidden.

A track qualifies when:

- it's named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**. A track you renamed doesn't qualify.
- it holds at least one clip, and only text clips.
- every one of those clips overlaps a clip being transcribed.

The last rule is about the whole track. If even one caption on it sits outside what **From:** covers, the track is left alone and **Replace:** won't list it. Choosing a wider **From:** can bring it in.

The old track's style doesn't matter, so **Replace:** also swaps out a Subtitles track or an [imported](/captions/import-captions/) one that meets these rules.

## Change a run of captions together

To change how captions look without changing their style, select them and use the inspector.

<Steps>

1. [Select the captions](/timeline/selecting-clips/) on the timeline.

2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.

3. Change what you need under [**Font**, **Style**](/text-and-shapes/text-style/), [**Outline**, **Backdrop**](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) or [**Box**](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).

</Steps>

Each page keeps its own words and word timing. Its word style stays too: the highlight colour, the pop and the pill only change by generating again, or through an agent. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#word-colours).

:::note
A change of **Font** on a word caption page, which a text preset also makes, means Re-lay Captions no longer recognises its track and [keeps it as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed).
:::

## Good to know

- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.

## With an agent

`transcribe` restyles the same way, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with `set_text`, which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).

## Related

- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)

input.content:
---
title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions pages them again for the new width, from the words they already hold.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />

## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

<Steps>

1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.

2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.

3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.

</Steps>

Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.

The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.

## What a re-lay keeps

Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.

Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:

- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
- Pages are never merged across clips, so a track you've split up can end up with more pages, but not fewer.
- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.

The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.

## Tracks kept as placed

A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."

Each track gets a line like this:

> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.

| The reason | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |

No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.

To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).

## When it is available, and inside a nest

The item is greyed out when:

- there's no caption track it can re-lay
- a sheet is open
- a recording is running

So if every caption track would be kept as placed, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why. The table above lists what to look for.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.

**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).

## Good to know

- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.

## With an agent

`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open. When nothing can be re-laid, it answers with each kept track and its reason, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)
- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)

---
title: Subtitles
description: Turn speech into classic two-line captions, give each speaker a colour, and see how the Caption preset sizes and places them on any canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Subtitles style turns speech into classic two-line cues, the kind you'd see on a film or a broadcast. Each cue is a text clip in the **Caption** preset.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style: ▸ Subtitles"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Nothing for the cues themselves. Speaker colours need AssemblyAI."
/>

<Shot
  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Style set to Subtitles. The three look checkboxes and Replace are greyed out, and the preview shows “This is how it looks” in small white text on a dark backdrop."
/>

## Make subtitles

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.

3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles**. The sheet opens on the last style you chose, and on Subtitles the first time.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

The cues land on a new track at the front of the stack, called **Captions**, or **Captions 2** and so on if that name is taken. The whole run is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.

## The Subtitles style

Frame Job builds each cue from the recognised words by these rules:

| Rule | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Lines in a cue | At most 2 |
| Characters on a line | At most 42 |
| Time on screen | At most 6 seconds, up to the end of the cue's last word |
| Gap between cues | At least one frame |
| Speakers in a cue | One. A change of speaker always starts a new cue. |

A cue starts on its first word and ends with its last, so it doesn't stay up through a long silence. A word too long for a line is left whole, never hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.

## Speaker colours

Each speaker's cues can take their own colour, so a viewer can tell who's talking.

<Steps>

1. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:** row is hidden with **On this Mac**.

2. Tick **Speakers:**, which reads "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles".

3. Set **Style:** to **Subtitles** and choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

Speakers take their colours in the order they first appear in the run: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. The fifth speaker is white like the first. The colours are a fixed table with no setting. To change one afterwards, select those cues and set the colour under **Text** in the [Clip tab](/text-and-shapes/text-style/).

Speakers are told apart within each media file, so the first speaker in one file and the first speaker in another count as two people and take two colours.

Speaker colours only apply to the Subtitles style. In a [word caption style](/captions/word-caption-styles/), a change of speaker starts a new page and the colours stay as the style draws them.

## The Caption preset

Every cue is drawn in the **Caption** [text preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), whether it was generated or [imported from a SubRip file](/captions/import-captions/).

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Typeface | Source Sans 3 Regular |
| Size | 3.5% of the canvas's shorter side |
| Alignment | Centred |
| Colour | White, unless a speaker colour applies |
| Backdrop | Black at 60%, with 12 px of padding and 8 px corners |
| Wraps at | 80% of the canvas width |
| Position on a wide or square canvas | The box is centred 38% of the frame height below the middle |
| Position on a canvas taller than wide | The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle |

On a 1920 × 1080 canvas that's 38 px text that wraps at 1,536 px. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas it's the same 38 px text, wrapping at 864 px, and a tall canvas such as 9:16 or 4:5 lifts the box to keep it clear of the bottom of the frame.

A narrow canvas can wrap a cue past two lines, because the wrap happens inside the box after the cue is built. On a canvas taller than wide, Frame Job counts these and tells you once the captions are placed:

> 3 captions wrap to more than two lines on this canvas.

After generating, this appears on the sheet, which stays open with **Close**. After importing, it's an alert. The captions are placed either way.

## Good to know

- An imported SubRip file keeps its own line breaks and timing. The rules in [The Subtitles style](#the-subtitles-style) only apply to generated cues.
- **Replace:** is greyed out with Subtitles chosen. To swap a word caption track for Subtitles, generate the new track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/).
- [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) keeps a Subtitles track as placed. To re-wrap one for a new canvas, generate it again on that canvas.
- A cue has no word timing, so the [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) don't apply. All three boxes are greyed out with Subtitles chosen.
- Subtitles are text in the picture, not a track a player can switch off. To ship a separate file, use [Export Captions…](/captions/export-captions/).

## With an agent

`transcribe` makes Subtitles unless it asks for another style, whatever the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

---
title: Word caption styles
description: Make the large word-by-word captions used in shorts and reels, choose how the spoken word is marked, and see how pages are filled for your canvas.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The five word styles make the large, one-row captions used in shorts and reels, where each word is marked as it's said.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Style:"
  tools="transcribe"
/>

## Make word captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Language:**, **Engine:** and **From:**. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) explains each one.

3. Set **Style:** to **Highlight**, **Pill**, **Karaoke**, **Build** or **One Word**. The sheet remembers your choice for next time.

4. Tick any [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/) you want, and check the [preview](#the-sheets-two-frame-preview).

5. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

## Word caption pages

A word style doesn't make cues. Each clip holds a **page** of words, with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. A page is still an ordinary [text clip](/captions/how-captions-work/), so you can drag, trim and split it.

All five styles are white with the spoken word marked. Words are marked by their timing only, so there's no keyword emphasis and no emoji.

The text is 7.5% of the canvas's shorter side, or 12% for One Word. That means a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height: on both 1080 × 1920 and 1920 × 1080 it's 81 px, or 130 px for One Word. Where a style pops the spoken word, the pop takes 0.12 s.

## The five styles

### Highlight

The spoken word turns yellow and pops to 112%, and the other words stay white.

Montserrat Black with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Pill

The spoken word sits on a violet pill, and doesn't change size. [Slide the pill](/captions/word-caption-looks/#slide-the-pill) makes the pill travel between words instead of jumping.

Montserrat ExtraBold, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### Karaoke

Words turn yellow as they're said and stay yellow. Words still to come are white at 55%.

Montserrat ExtraBold, as written. Karaoke can use up to two lines, and it's the only style that wraps a page of several words. The box is centred 28% of the frame height below the middle.

### Build

Words appear one by one. The newest is yellow and pops to 115%, and the ones before it are white.

Anton with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred a quarter of the frame height below the middle.

### One Word

One large word at a time, white, popping to 120%. Every page holds one word.

Bebas Neue with a black outline, in capitals. The box is centred 18% of the frame height below the middle.

## Bundled typefaces

Montserrat Black, Montserrat ExtraBold, Anton and Bebas Neue ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License, so there's nothing to install.

## Pages are filled to their measured width

A page holds as many words as fit, not a set number. Frame Job measures each page in its style's typeface, size, case and outline on your canvas, and fills it up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line. Karaoke can use two lines, and One Word always holds one word.

So the same speech makes shorter pages on a 9:16 canvas than on a 16:9 one. On a 1080 × 1920 canvas a page can be about 929 px wide. If you change the canvas size later, [Re-lay Captions for This Canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/) fills the pages again.

When a page fills up by width and the next page would be much shorter, Frame Job can move the last word across so the two come closer in width. That stops a sentence ending on one word alone.

## Where a page breaks

A page ends early at any of these:

- a pause of 0.25 s or more between two words
- a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`
- 3 seconds on screen, up to the end of the page's last word
- a change of speaker, when [**Speakers:**](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) is ticked

When the width runs out within two words of a comma, semicolon or colon, the break moves back to that mark. It only does this when the page is already at least half full and the words that move still fit on the next page.

On-device words rarely carry a pause, because the recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it. Pages from **On this Mac** break at pauses less often than pages from AssemblyAI.

## A word too wide for the frame

A word too wide for a page gets a page of its own and shrinks in 5% steps, down to 80% of the style's size, until it fits. If it's still too wide at 80%, it stays at that size and wraps.

## How long a page stays up

A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, and the row is empty until the next page. If the next page starts sooner than that, the page runs right up to it, so the row doesn't blink between pages.

Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.

## The sheet's two-frame preview

The preview under the looks shows a sample page, drawn the way the canvas draws it and paged for this canvas's proportions. It shows you how the style looks, not how big it will be, because each frame is scaled to fit the strip.

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Two frames | A word style, with the first word active in the top frame and the second word in the bottom one. A page of one word shows that word in both. |
| One frame | Subtitles. |
| The sample words | The first words of the first clip's cached AssemblyAI transcript when there is one, otherwise "This is how it looks". |
| A half-filled word | **Fill words as spoken** is ticked. |
| A pill between two words | **Slide the pill** is ticked. It shows in the second frame. |

**Dim in pauses** isn't previewed.

## Good to know

- A style is set when the captions are generated, and you can't switch it on a placed track. To change it, see [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
- The capitals are applied when a page is drawn, so the words stay as written in the **Content** box and in an [exported caption file](/captions/export-captions/). To show a page as written, untick **UPPERCASE**. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/).
- [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) don't apply to a timed page.
- The [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style is the sixth choice in the **Style:** pop-up, and it works differently: two-line cues with no word timing.

## With an agent

`transcribe` makes word captions when it asks for a word style. It never uses the style the sheet last chose. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

---
title: Looks for word captions
description: Add a sliding pill, a left-to-right word fill or a dim in pauses to word captions, and find out what you can change about their colours.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Looks add movement to a [word style](/captions/word-caption-styles/)'s pages: a pill that slides between words, a word that fills as it's said, and a page that dims when nobody's talking.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="The Generate Captions sheet, under Style:"
  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
/>

## Three looks for word captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Style:** to a word style.

3. Tick the looks you want under the **Style:** pop-up.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

Each look works with some styles and not others:

| Look | Highlight | Pill | Karaoke | Build | One Word |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Slide the pill** | | Yes | | | |
| **Fill words as spoken** | Yes | | Yes | Yes | |
| **Dim in pauses** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

A box that doesn't apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but it keeps its tick for when you switch back. With **Subtitles** chosen, all three are greyed out.

Each box is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs.

A look changes how a word is drawn, never a letter or the size of the page. Ticking one doesn't change where pages break.

Looks are set when the captions are generated, like the style. To change them on a placed track, [generate again with Replace](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again).

## Slide the pill

The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, instead of jumping. The slide takes 0.2 s, or less when the next word starts sooner, so the pill has always arrived before it has to leave. The first word on a page has nothing to slide from, so the pill starts there.

This works with **Pill**, the only style that has one.

## Fill words as spoken

The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken. The fill runs from the word's start to its end, and takes 0.6 s at most, so a long word finishes filling before it's finished being said.

| Style | The part already said | The rest of the word |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Highlight** | Yellow | White |
| **Karaoke** | Yellow | White at 55% |
| **Build** | Yellow | Not drawn yet |

**Pill** and **One Word** can't use this look, because their spoken word is the same colour on both sides of the fill.

## Dim in pauses

The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. Each fade takes 0.1 s, and the words and the pill fade together. It works with all five word styles.

The page also dims:

- before the first word, when that word starts late. The page opens dim, with no fade.
- after the last word, until the caption ends.

A pause of 0.25 s also [ends a page](/captions/word-caption-styles/#where-a-page-breaks), so on a generated track you'll mostly see the dim at the end of a page, after its last word.

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.

The sheet's [preview](/captions/word-caption-styles/#the-sheets-two-frame-preview) doesn't show this look.

## Word colours

The inspector has no section for a page's word colours, pop size or pill. Nothing in the Clip tab changes the yellow, the violet or how far the word pops.

To change them, generate again with a [different style](/captions/restyle-captions/#restyle-by-generating-again), or have an agent do it.

The **Color** row under **Text ▸ Style** still works. It changes the words drawn in the text's own colour, such as the unmarked words in **Highlight**, and leaves the marked word as it is.

## With an agent

An agent can do two things here that the sheet can't.

It can change a placed page's word style with `set_text`. That covers highlighting or building word by word, the colours of the spoken word and of the words before and after it, a pop from 100% to 150%, the pill's colour, padding and corners, and how far the page dims, from none to fully invisible. The sheet's dim is always half. A page changed this way is no longer one of the styles Frame Job makes, so [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed) keeps its track as placed. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).

It can also ask for looks with `transcribe`, but each one is off unless it asks, never what the sheet last chose. Frame Job won't add a look to a style it wouldn't show on. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
- [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

---
title: Restyle a caption track
description: Switch a caption track to another word style or look by generating it again, or change the font and backdrop of a run of captions in the inspector.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

There are two ways to restyle captions, depending on what you want to change. A word style and its looks are set when the captions are generated, so changing those means generating again. Font, outline and backdrop are ordinary text settings, which you can change on a run of captions in the inspector.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where={['The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Replace:', 'Clip tab ▸ Text']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
/>

## Restyle by generating again

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and set **From:** to the same clips.

2. Choose the new word style and [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/).

3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front of the stack, all in one undo step, **Generate Captions**. The new track takes the first free name, so a lone **Captions** track is replaced by another called **Captions**.

What it costs depends on the engine:

- **AssemblyAI:** the cached transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
- **On this Mac:** the audio is recognised again. It's free, but it takes the time again.

:::caution
New pages are made from the transcript, not from the old track. Words you corrected, pages you split or trimmed, and anything you restyled by hand go with the old track. To page a track again and keep your corrections, use [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) instead.
:::

## Which tracks Replace may remove

**Replace:** is live only for a word style, and only when there's a track it may replace. It's greyed out with Subtitles chosen. When it isn't live, it's unticked and the line under it is hidden.

A track qualifies when:

- it's named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**. A track you renamed doesn't qualify.
- it holds at least one clip, and only text clips.
- every one of those clips overlaps a clip being transcribed.

The last rule is about the whole track. If even one caption on it sits outside what **From:** covers, the track is left alone and **Replace:** won't list it. Choosing a wider **From:** can bring it in.

The old track's style doesn't matter, so **Replace:** also swaps out a Subtitles track or an [imported](/captions/import-captions/) one that meets these rules.

## Change a run of captions together

To change how captions look without changing their style, select them and use the inspector.

<Steps>

1. [Select the captions](/timeline/selecting-clips/) on the timeline.

2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.

3. Change what you need under [**Font**, **Style**](/text-and-shapes/text-style/), [**Outline**, **Backdrop**](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) or [**Box**](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).

</Steps>

Each page keeps its own words and word timing. Its word style stays too: the highlight colour, the pop and the pill only change by generating again, or through an agent. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#word-colours).

:::note
A change of **Font** on a word caption page, which a text preset also makes, means Re-lay Captions no longer recognises its track and [keeps it as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed).
:::

## Good to know

- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.

## With an agent

`transcribe` restyles the same way, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with `set_text`, which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).

title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions pages them again for the new width, from the words they already hold.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />

## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas

<Steps>

1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.

2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.

3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.

</Steps>

Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.

The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.

## What a re-lay keeps

Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.

Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:

- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
- Pages are never merged across clips, so a track you've split up can end up with more pages, but not fewer.
- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.

The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.

## Tracks kept as placed

A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."

Each track gets a line like this:

> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.

| The reason | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |

No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.

To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).

## When it is available, and inside a nest

The item is greyed out when:

- there's no caption track it can re-lay
- a sheet is open
- a recording is running

So if every caption track would be kept as placed, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why. The table above lists what to look for.

Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.

**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).

## Good to know

- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.

## With an agent

`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open. When nothing can be re-laid, it answers with each kept track and its reason, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
